_meta.indication: Treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis), and esophageal candidiasis.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority, multicenter study of anidulafungin versus fluconazole; patients randomized 1:1 to anidulafungin IV (200 mg loading, then 100 mg daily) or fluconazole IV (800 mg loading, 400 mg maintenance).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis (primarily non-neutropenic).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was the global response (combined clinical and microbiological) in the microbiological intent-to-treat (Micro-ITT/MITT) population at the end of IV therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 261 patients randomized; MITT population 245 (127 anidulafungin, 118 fluconazole).
pivotal_trials.result: Global response at end of IV therapy (MITT): 75.6% anidulafungin vs 60.2% fluconazole; between-group difference 15.4% (95% CI 3.0, 27.8), meeting non-inferiority (margin -20%) and establishing statistical superiority since the lower bound exceeded 0.

key_safety: Generally well tolerated; most frequent treatment-related AEs in the candidemia study (anidulafungin vs fluconazole) were diarrhea (3.1% vs 1.6%) and hypokalemia (3.1% vs 2.4%). Possible infusion-related reactions occurred (28 (13.2%) and 9 (7%) patients in the integrated analysis of safety). Hepatic effects are the main safety concern; a few cases of significant hepatic dysfunction and hepatitis were reported in patients receiving anidulafungin in studies completed since the original NDA submission, though a causal relationship to anidulafungin was not established.
target_moa: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin (lipopeptide) that non-competitively inhibits 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase, blocking formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall not present in mammalian cells.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not required.

basis.text: A six month priority review was granted for the candidemia/invasive candidiasis indication.

citations.quote: A six month priority review was granted for this indication.

summary.text: NDA 21-948 for anidulafungin (Eraxis) in candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis was submitted and received August 18, 2005 and granted a six-month priority review; an advisory committee was not required, and the application was approved based on the single pivotal study VER002-9. A deferred pediatric study was required under PREA as a postmarketing commitment.

citations.quote: NDA 21-948 was submitted on August 18, 2005 and received on August 18, 2005.
A six month priority review was granted for this indication.
An advisory committee was not required.
One pivotal study, VER002-9, has been submitted to provide support for the use of anidulafungin in the treatment of candidemia.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis) in pediatric patients ages zero months to sixteen years; final report submission February 17, 2011.
